h1: Horizontal press brakes — NC hydraulic horizontal presses, 11 to 165 US tons
intro: A horizontal press brake is a hydraulic press laid on its side: the ram pushes the tool across a heavy steel table at bench height, so flat bar, angle, channel, pipe, solid bar and busbar lie flat in front of the operator while they are bent, punched, sheared, notched or straightened. With the right tooling one machine does the work of a small press brake, a bar bender, a heavy-wall pipe bender, a punch and a straightening press — the workhorse of maintenance and repair shops, gate, railing and fence makers, trailer and agricultural fabricators and the switchgear builders who bend copper busbar. NovoTech sells the HP series of Tubend, built in Bursa, Turkey: six NC-controlled models from the 11-ton HP 10 to the 110-ton HP 100, and the 132- and 165-ton HP 120 and HP 150 with a T-slot table and hardened support columns for straightening heavy sections. Every HP has a touch-screen control stand with manual, automatic and recipe modes and a foot pedal; a servo NC back gauge, a library of bending, punching, shearing, pipe and busbar tools and dies made for your part are available. Installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What is a horizontal press brake used for?
faq.a: Bending, punching, shearing, notching and straightening bar stock with the part lying flat on a table at bench height. The ram moves horizontally, so long parts rest on the table and the operator watches the bend from the side. With its tooling one HP replaces a small press brake for flat bar, a bar and pipe bender, a punch and a straightening press: brackets and clamps, U-bolts and hooks, gate and railing parts, pipe saddles and offsets, reduced and expanded pipe ends, bent and punched copper busbar.

faq.q: Which HP size do I need?
faq.a: Size the press by the heaviest flat bar you bend the hard way in mild steel: HP 10 – 5-7/8″ × 1/4″, HP 20 – 7-7/8″ × 3/8″, HP 40 – 9-7/8″ × 5/8″, HP 60 – 11-13/16″ × 5/8″, HP 80 – 11-13/16″ × 13/16″, HP 100 – 11-13/16″ × 15/16″, HP 120 and HP 150 – 19-11/16″ × 1-3/16″ and 1-9/16″. Punching takes the most force: a Ø13/16″ hole in 1/2″ mild steel needs about 32 US tons, so an HP 40 or larger. Stainless steel needs about 1.5 times the force of mild steel.

faq.q: How does the NC control work?
faq.a: On the touch-screen of the control stand. In manual mode the ram works between the minimum and maximum stroke you set, while the pedal is pressed — for setting up and single parts. The automatic modes repeat the stroke cycle by cycle for series parts. In recipe mode a part with several operations is stored as a list of positions and run step by step; recipes are saved and reloaded for the next batch.

faq.q: What does the automatic back gauge add?
faq.a: A servo-driven NC back gauge, 3.3, 6.6 or 9.8 ft (1, 2 or 3 m) long, positions the part for every step of a recipe, so parts with several bends or holes at set distances come off faster and more repeatably than with a manual stop. Its pull-back retracts the stop while the part bends, so a part that swings against the gauge during the bend is not pushed off position.

Bending tools — radius punch with V-die, press brake punch and bolt punch with multi-V dies, narrow V-die, two-sided V and spring-loaded U-bending tools, profile and round bar bending tools; pipe tools — mandrel-less pipe bending, solid bar and thick-wall pipe bending, pipe end reduction and expansion, pipe clamping and pipe notching; wide-radius bending, straightening, punching and shearing tools; and busbar tools for shearing, punching, precision, vertical and Z-bending, corner notching and twisting. Dies are also designed and made for your part — send us the drawing.

Yes — with the busbar tools the HP shears, punches, bends flat and on edge, Z-bends, corner-notches and twists copper and aluminum busbar for switchgear, panel and battery builders, and the recipe mode repeats a busbar with several operations the same way every time.

faq.q: What power supply does an HP press need?
faq.a: Three-phase: the HP presses are supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved panel as standard, and for 208 V, 240 V or 480 V 3-phase on request. Motors run from 1.5 HP on the HP 10 to 15 HP on the HP 100 and 10 HP on the HP 150.
